cohort: 273 patients who underwent laparoscopic myomectomy (n=222) or robotic myomectomy (n=51) followed by subsequent cesarean delivery
finding: Although more and larger myomas were removed during robotic myomectomy compared to laparoscopic myomectomy, there were no significant differences in cesarean delivery outcomes or adhesion formation between the two groups.
mod_finding: Although more myomas were removed during robotic myomectomy compared to laparoscopic myomectomy, cesarean delivery outcomes and adhesion formation were similar between the two groups.
